extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Amended Final Order applying 37 C.F.R. §11.24 to impose reciprocal discipline (stayed suspension and probation) based on a state bar's probated suspension, and setting notice, reporting, and publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state bar under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order requests imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Texas State Bar's District 9 Grievance Committee. A respondent is given an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline as provided in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate violation — 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: A violation of 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h) is predicated upon being disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state; such a state disciplinary determination can support reciprocal discipline before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Amended Final Order states Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on his violation of §11.804(h), having been disciplined by the Texas State Bar. Use the state determination as the basis for USPTO action under §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service procedures (certified mail and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order initiating reciprocal-discipline proceedings must be sent to the respondent (here sent by certified mail) and must inform the respondent of the complaint and the opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. provided) and delivered on March 28, 2018. The Notice provided 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline under §11.24(d)(1). Maintain service records (e.g., certified-mail receipt numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of respondent's failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and Respondent's stayed suspension ... is the appropriate discipline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed: stayed suspension and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may order suspension from practice before the USPTO for a specified period, and may stay that suspension while placing the practitioner on probation for the same period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, the Respondent is suspended for thirty (30) months with the suspension stayed, and placed on probation for thirty (30) months, both commencing on the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with state's Terms of Probation
rubrics_metrics.description: When imposing reciprocal probation, the respondent must comply with the terms and conditions of the state-imposed probated suspension as a condition of USPTO probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires Respondent to comply with the 13 'Terms of Probation' set forth in the August 30, 2017 Agreed Judgment Order (examples include: not violate the Agreed Judgment Order; not engage in professional misconduct; keep State Bar notified of current addresses and telephone numbers; comply with MCLE and IOLTA requirements; promptly respond to requests from Chief Disciplinary Counsel; pay reasonable attorney's fees and expenses; engage an independent CPA to assist with trust account records; CPA reviews every six months; report results to State Bar; provide reports and verifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent obligation to report state probation revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must notify the USPTO/OED of any decision by the state bar to revoke the state probation, including the terms of any probation revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly requires Respondent to provide notice of any decision by the Texas State Bar to revoke the Texas probation, as set forth in the Agreed Judgment Order, including terms of any revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the Office's final discipline notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to publish a Notice materially consistent with the sample text provided in the Order (sample text summarizes the suspension, probation, predicate rule violated §11.804(h), misconduct facts, and availability of disciplinary decisions at the OED FOIA Reading Room). Use the sample wording as a template for Official Gazette publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs compliance with §11.59 for dissemination to relevant state disciplinary agencies, courts of admission, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/implication of a 'fully probated suspension' (state bar context)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'fully probated suspension' (per State Bar of Texas) allows a lawyer to practice law during the period of suspension but requires compliance with specific terms of probation throughout the probated suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the State Bar of Texas' explanation that a fully probated suspension permits practice while imposing probationary terms; those state terms are incorporated into USPTO probation where reciprocal discipline is adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides the URL for the OED FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) where disciplinary decisions are posted for public inspection.
